doc: The Claude Code CLI's own names. The SDK emits no in-process telemetry; the CLI it spawns self-instruments, so these are the CLI's vocabulary.

carriers.doc: The turns and tool results handed to the model, tagged in-band.
The system prompt, reported beside the conversation: a detached request frame.
The tool a span was asked to run, alongside its input.

detect.doc: The CLI subprocess emits every span under one prefix. Two service names because the CLI reports one and the host process wrapping it reports the other.
detect.label: ClaudeAgentSDK

messages.doc: The caller-supplied system prompt, emitted once per session rather than per request. Blank counts as absent here: this dialect writes the attribute whether or not there is a prompt.

Either side of the conversation, in one attribute, distinguished by a bracketed tag - and several sections joined by a separator, one per parallel tool call, each read on its own so every result keeps its own id.

routes.doc: A tool result. The tag's remainder is the call id, which is what pairs the result with its tool_use block rather than leaving it to be guessed from content. The name-tagged form is the same result as raw structured telemetry, so it is dropped - narrowly: only when the capture lacks the id prefix *and* the body opens as JSON, so if that prefix changes an unrecognised section still reaches the feed unlinked instead of vanishing.
Anything else is the user's turn - including an unrecognised tag, which is read rather than discarded.

messages.doc: A tool call rebuilt from the tool span. The read carrier is the tool's *name*, which becomes the block's name member; the input is attached from another attribute where the payload sits under a bracketed tag naming the tool, so it is stripped before parsing - parsing without stripping fails and the member would silently fall back to its empty form. An unparseable input does fall back to `{}`, because the block's shape requires the member.

message_events.name: tool.output
message_events.doc: The CLI's tool result body, emitted only with tool-content logging enabled - which is why no captured fixture exercises it, and why a unit test is what holds it.

event_roles.name: tool.output
event_roles.doc: This dialect's CLI writes a tool result body on its own span event rather than on a convention event, so the name is the only thing that says the message is a tool's answer. Needs `OTEL_LOG_TOOL_CONTENT=1`.
